findings.issue: The old Debian payload overlaps installed official packages.
findings.baseline: 1.177-15: two files overlap obscura-cli and seven overlap obscura-gui.
findings.resolution: Separate executable paths, service, group, state directories, desktop/icon/AppStream/AppArmor identities; installation scripts never start or stop the official backend.
findings.verification: Real 1.177-16 .deb ownership intersection is empty. APT simulation installs only obscura-simple with zero removals.

findings.issue: Renaming the package alone leaves shared runtime IPC, GUI identity, autostart and user storage.
findings.resolution: Compile-time simple-client feature isolates sockets, systemd queries, GTK/tray IDs, autostart, operator command and WebKit data/cache. Protocol version checks retained. Shared /run/obscura.lock intentionally retained before network setup.
findings.verification: Rust namespace/autostart/exclusive-lock tests pass. Real CLI and GUI traces contact only Simple sockets; native D-Bus ownership and log namespace verified. Official process 65397 observed holding the shared lock.

findings.issue: Community UI, metadata and support links ambiguously identify the fork as the official app.
findings.resolution: Obscura Simple (Unofficial) launcher/window/tray, explicit community About/Help text, correct recovery service commands, own AppStream metadata without official Alpha screenshots.
findings.verification: UI branding regression test passes; actual final packaged GUI displays the separated-service warning and Simple journal command.

rust.ignored_reason: Kernel/TUN/network namespace integration tests intentionally not run on the live VPN host.

flatpak.scope: GUI only, requires matching Simple host service from the .deb
flatpak.unix_socket_mount_probe: Passed read-only Unix socket mount and peer UID preservation with an isolated transport fixture, not a VPN API fixture or live connection.

verification.native_scope: Final packaged .deb and Flatpak GUIs, isolated D-Bus/Xvfb/user directories, unavailable Simple service screens. No login, repair, connection, kill-switch or account operations were performed.

limitations: No live VPN handover, reboot or kernel/network integration tests were performed.

Debian installation was simulated, not executed. Flatpak was installed into an isolated user installation for verification. Official and Simple packages may coexist; simultaneous backends are intentionally excluded.
Simple service is disabled by default. Boot protection requires explicit configuration; historical boot-test results do not validate this new passive default.
Legacy package purge scripts can still affect the official service before migration. No old shared state or credentials were deleted or copied.
